segments.it: «Nonna Lucia, tu avevi il **registro** a scuola?»
segments.en: “Grandma Lucia, did you have the **class register** at school?”

segments.it: «Io ho insegnato trentacinque anni» dice Lucia. «Trentacinque anni dietro la **cattedra**.»
segments.en: “I taught for thirty-five years,” says Lucia. “Thirty-five years behind the **teacher's desk**.”

segments.it: «E il **registro**?»
segments.en: “And the **class register**?”

segments.it: «Il **registro** era la mia vita» risponde lei. «E a giugno arrivava la **pagella**.»
segments.en: “The **class register** was my life,” she answers. “And in June the **report card** arrived.”

segments.it: «E gli alunni erano **severi**?» chiede Leo.
segments.en: “And were the pupils **strict**?” asks Leo.

segments.it: «No, gli alunni no. La maestra era **severa**» dice Lucia. «E gli alunni dovevano **obbedire**.»
segments.en: “No, not the pupils. The teacher was **strict**,” says Lucia. “And the pupils had to **obey**.”
voice: No, gli alunni no. La maestra era **severa**

segments.it: «Tutti?»
segments.en: “All of them?”

segments.it: «Quasi tutti» dice Lucia. «Qualcuno, **ogni estate**, tornava a settembre e dimenticava tutto.»
segments.en: “Almost all of them,” says Lucia. “Someone, **every summer**, came back in September and forgot everything.”
voice: Qualcuno, **ogni estate**, tornava a settembre e dimenticava tutto.

segments.it: «Ogni estate, in macchina, verso la Liguria, io e Matteo dovevamo imparare a memoria una poesia.»

segments.it: «Una **poesia**?» chiede Matteo. «Io ricordo una **filastrocca**.»
segments.en: “A **poem**?” asks Matteo. “I remember a **nursery rhyme**.”

segments.it: «Una **poesia**» ripete Chiara. «La mamma aveva il libro sul cruscotto.»
segments.en: “A **poem**,” repeats Chiara. “Mom had the book on the dashboard.”
voice: La mamma aveva il libro sul cruscotto.

segments.it: «No, era una **filastrocca** sui mesi» dice Matteo. «E io la dicevo tutta, anche a luglio.»
segments.en: “No, it was a **nursery rhyme** about the months,” says Matteo. “And I recited the whole thing, even in July.”
voice: E io la dicevo tutta, anche a luglio.

segments.it: «Era **agosto**, non luglio. Sempre **agosto**» dice Chiara.
segments.en: “It was **August**, not July. Always **August**,” says Chiara.

segments.it: «E dove andavamo? In **pensione** o in un appartamento?»

segments.it: «In **pensione**, naturalmente» dice lei. «Con la signora Elena e il cane piccolo.»
segments.en: “To a **guesthouse**, of course,” she says. “With signora Elena and the little dog.”

segments.en: “It wasn't a **guesthouse**, it was a rented house,” says Matteo.

segments.en: “By car, always by car,” says Matteo. “The blue one.”

segments.en: “The car was red,” says Chiara.

segments.it: «Blu» dice Matteo.
segments.en: “Blue,” says Matteo.

segments.it: «Rossa» dice Chiara.
segments.en: “Red,” says Chiara.

segments.en: “And what seat did I have on the **journey**?” asks Matteo. “Always in the back, always in the middle.”

segments.it: «Perché tu dormivi e io guardavo la strada» dice Chiara.
segments.en: “Because you slept and I watched the road,” says Chiara.

segments.en: “Can I say something?” asks Kevin.

segments.en: “We too, **every summer**, **used to go** to a lake,” says Kevin. “In Ohio there's a big lake.”

segments.it: «Ah. Al lago» ripete Kevin.
segments.en: “Ah. To the lake,” repeats Kevin.

segments.en: “Yes, but it was different,” says Kevin. “No **guesthouse**. A wooden house.”

segments.en: “Wooden?” asks Leo.

segments.it: «Di legno. Con il camino» dice Kevin.
segments.en: “Wooden. With a fireplace,” says Kevin.

segments.en: “And did you have the **dairy shop** nearby?” asks Leo.

segments.en: “The what?” asks Kevin.

segments.it: «Basta con la **villeggiatura**» dice. «Mangiate.»
